searchText: heya all 👋 not sure what the right channel is for this so pardon me and plz feel free to redirect so quick question re: `lodestar` client configuration files it looks like the `--rcConfig` flag points to a (*yaml or json*) file which should contain cli options minus the preceding `--` as config options, which makes sense tho not quite sure what the `beacon --configFile` flag should point to seems as tho the client doesn't process global or beacon specific options (a bit more detail @ https://discord.com/channels/593655374469660673/743858262864167062/935668034092290078 if interested) yes, options in format of key: value pair hmm <@!792822129019584562> not sure I understand any cli argument is key (without --), value is what you would provide as arg value right, makes sense for the rcConfig but missing what goes in the `beacon --configFile` you don't need --configFile so it has no purpose? although you can provide json nested input args in it i mean, i'm working on some infra to support automation w/r/t operating a lodestar client oh ok sort of deprecated is the better word ah ok .. and replaced by rcConfig? but essentially you can do chain: {blah1,blah2} to provide chain.blah1 chain.blah2 args yes, rcConfig is better as there is no confusion for how args are being mapped in a nested structure in --configFile (and some args are not mapped, so even more confusion for a user) --rcConfig is a cleaner interface rcConfig example: ``` rootDir: /data/interop/datadir/lodestar paramsFile: /data/interop/datadir/testnet/config.yaml genesisStateFile: /data/interop/datadir/testnet/genesis.ssz network.discv5.enabled: true network.discv5.bootEnrs: - enr:-Ly4QPOzB5o4ldodVGk2MK9ms-E8NL6NYHBz8xGBiy-am9vYZ0zHX7TQDM--XtLb48jg9N6oOdMvwBmZ3DtDFY9dmzcCh2F0dG5ldHOIAAAAAAAAAACEZXRoMpCSRWn8AgAAAf__________gmlkgnY0gmlwhH8AAAGJc2VjcDI1NmsxoQJmMbzA19NBqAFPuBQZiLsQT-BQ1FOQyzElspkbYm2JSYhzeW5jbmV0cwCDdGNwgiMog3VkcIIjKA eth1.disableEth1DepositDataTracker: true eth1.enabled: false execution.urls: http://localhost:8545 enr.ip: 127.0.0.1 enr.tcp: 9001 enr.udp: 9001 port: 9001 discoveryPort: 9001 ``` oh ok copy that right on thx!
